title: Inverting Op-Amp: The Virtual Short Does the Algebra
topic: Inverting op-amp — V+ grounded, V− driven to a virtual ground by feedback, KCL at the summing junction gives V_out = −(R_f/R_in)·V_in; the op-amp's own gain never enters the answer because the feedback loop forces V− to match V+

beats.narration: An op-amp gain is enormous and not well controlled — yet you can build a precise amplifier from one. How?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
Sloppy gain, precise amplifier — how?

beats.narration: Here's the inverting configuration. V plus sits at ground. The input drives V minus through R in, and R f closes a loop from the output back to V minus.

elements.content: Op-amp triangle with V−, V+, V_out pins
V+ pin tied to ground symbol
V_in source on the left going through R_in into V−
R_f feedback resistor from V_out back to V−
Pin labels: V−, V+, V_out, R_in, R_f, V_in
input through R_in, feedback through R_f — that's the whole story

beats.narration: Because the gain is huge, the op-amp will adjust V out by whatever amount it takes to drag V minus back to the same voltage as V plus — which is ground. V minus is a virtual ground.

elements.content: Glowing pulse on V− showing feedback driving it to 0
V− ≈ V+ = 0  (virtual ground)
feedback drags V_minus to V_plus — no current goes into the op-amp itself

beats.narration: Apply Kirchhoff's current law at V minus. The current arriving from V in equals the current leaving towards V out. Solve, and the output is minus R f over R in times the input.

elements.content: Flowing current dots through R_in (into V−) and R_f (out to V_out)
V_in / R_in = −V_out / R_f
V_out = −(R_f / R_in) · V_in
two resistors set the gain — the op-amp itself doesn't appear

beats.narration: Sweep the input — the output moves opposite, scaled by the resistor ratio.

elements.content: Time axis showing V_in (top trace) and V_out (bottom trace, inverted and scaled)
V_in sinusoidal in chalk; V_out a mirror of V_in scaled by R_f/R_in in amber
gain = −R_f / R_in
flip the sign, scale by the ratio — and the op-amp's huge gain never appears
